subject: Business Models
title: Access Over Ownership
description: A quick win: understand Access Over Ownership.

hook.text: You don't own your Spotify music, your Kindle books, or your Netflix movies. You rent access to everything.

buildup.text: The ownership model is shifting: subscriptions replace purchases across music, software, cars, and even clothing.

discovery.text: Companies prefer subscriptions: predictable revenue, ongoing relationships, and the ability to revoke access.

twist.text: When services shut down, your 'owned' content vanishes. Google has killed 275+ products, taking user data with them.

climax.text: Access is convenient but fragile. Ownership is permanent but expensive. The market is choosing convenience.

punchline.text: You own nothing, access everything. Convenient until the service shuts down.

quiz.question: What is the risk of the access-over-ownership model for consumers?
options: Content disappears when services shut down since you don't truly own it
